title: Deductible applied to patient
plain: The payer did not pay this amount because it was applied to the patient's unmet annual deductible. The patient, not the plan, is responsible for this portion of the bill.
causes: The patient has not yet met the plan-year deductible
The claim was processed before the deductible was satisfied
The patient's deductible balance was recorded incorrectly by the payer
fix: Confirm the remaining deductible balance with the payer or through eligibility verification
Bill the patient for the deductible amount
Offer a payment plan or financial assistance if needed
If the deductible was already met, send proof and request reprocessing

title: Coinsurance applied to patient
plain: Under the plan's cost-sharing design, the patient owes a set percentage of the allowed amount for this service and the plan pays the rest — that patient percentage is what this adjustment shows. Whether it applies before or after the deductible depends on the plan. It is not a denial of the service itself.
causes: The plan's coinsurance percentage applies to this service
The service is covered but subject to cost sharing
The claim was priced at the allowed amount and split per the benefit design
fix: Verify the coinsurance percentage and allowed amount on the remittance
Bill the patient for their share
Check whether a secondary plan or supplemental policy covers the balance
If the percentage looks wrong, ask the payer to reprice the claim

title: Copay applied to patient
plain: This is the fixed dollar copay the patient owes for the visit or service under their plan. The payer withheld it from the payment because it is the patient's responsibility.
causes: A flat copay applies to this service type
The patient has not paid the copay at the time of service
A copay was applied in addition to other cost sharing
fix: Collect the copay from the patient (point of service is ideal)
Bill the patient if the copay was not collected
Verify the copay amount against the plan's benefit summary
Confirm no duplicate copay was taken for the same date of service

title: Modifier doesn't match procedure code
plain: The payer says the modifier submitted with this procedure code is not a valid or appropriate combination. The service may be legitimate, but the coding as billed does not line up.
causes: The modifier billed is not valid with, or not allowed on, this procedure code
The payer requires a different modifier for the same service
The wrong modifier was reported for the service actually performed
fix: Review the code-modifier pair against current CPT/AMA guidance and the payer's policy
Correct the modifier and submit a corrected claim
Attach the operative note or procedure documentation if the payer requires it
If the coding is already correct, appeal with supporting documentation

title: Place of service inconsistency
plain: The place of service or the type of bill on the claim does not match how the payer expects this procedure to be billed. The service itself is not in question — the setting information is.
causes: Wrong place of service code reported for where the service was furnished
Type of bill is not valid for the setting (for example, facility vs. non-facility)
Telehealth or off-site service billed without the payer's required setting code
fix: Confirm where the service actually took place and compare it to the place of service billed
Correct the place of service or type of bill and submit a corrected claim
Check the payer's current policy for telehealth and non-facility billing
If the original coding was right, appeal with documentation of the setting

title: Procedure code conflicts with patient age
plain: The payer says this procedure or revenue code is not consistent with the patient's age on file. Either the code is outside the covered age range or the age itself is wrong.
causes: The procedure is age-restricted and the patient falls outside the covered range
A pediatric or adult-only code was billed for the wrong age group
The patient's date of birth in the payer's system does not match the chart
fix: Verify the patient's date of birth on the claim against the chart and the payer's records
Check the payer's age limits for the procedure or revenue code
Correct the age or replace the code and resubmit
If the patient does meet criteria, appeal with clinical documentation

title: Procedure code conflicts with patient gender
plain: The payer flagged this procedure or revenue code as not matching the patient's gender on file. This is usually a data mismatch rather than a problem with the care that was given.
causes: The procedure is gender-specific and the gender on the claim does not match
The member's gender is recorded incorrectly in the payer's system
A code was selected that is restricted to a different gender
fix: Confirm the patient's gender in the chart and with the payer
Update the payer's member record if it is wrong
Correct the claim or the procedure code and resubmit
Appeal with clinical documentation if the service was appropriate

title: Provider specialty doesn't match procedure
plain: The payer says the billing or rendering provider's specialty or taxonomy does not support this procedure code. Typically the provider is not credentialed or enrolled for that service type.
causes: The taxonomy or specialty code on the claim does not match the service billed
The provider is not enrolled or credentialed with the payer for this service
The wrong NPI or taxonomy was reported on the claim
fix: Check the provider's taxonomy code on the claim against payer enrollment records
Correct the taxonomy, NPI, or rendering provider and resubmit
Contact credentialing to add the missing specialty or service category
Appeal with proof of credentials or training if the service is within scope

title: Diagnosis doesn't match patient age
plain: The diagnosis on the claim is not considered consistent with the patient's age, so the payer will not link it to the service. This often points to a date-of-birth or diagnosis code error.
causes: The diagnosis code is age-specific and the patient's age does not fit
The patient's date of birth on the claim is incorrect
The wrong diagnosis was linked to the procedure on the claim
fix: Verify the patient's date of birth on the claim against the chart
Review the diagnosis codes for age-specific validity
Correct the date of birth or diagnosis and submit a corrected claim
Appeal with chart notes if the diagnosis is accurate as coded

title: Diagnosis doesn't match patient gender
plain: The payer says the diagnosis code is not consistent with the patient's gender on file, so it will not support the service billed. This is usually a demographic or code-selection error.
causes: The diagnosis is gender-specific and does not match the gender on the claim
The member's gender is recorded incorrectly by the payer
An incorrect diagnosis code was linked to the procedure
fix: Confirm the patient's gender in the chart and with the payer
Update the payer's member record if the gender is wrong
Correct the diagnosis or demographic data and resubmit the claim
Appeal with clinical documentation if the coding is accurate

title: Diagnosis does not match procedure
plain: The diagnosis code billed does not support or align with the procedure or service performed, according to the payer's review.
causes: Wrong diagnosis linked to the procedure
Incorrect procedure code billed
Diagnosis code too general or unspecified
Payer edit sees a clinical mismatch
fix: Check the medical record for the correct diagnosis and procedure
Correct the ICD-10/CPT linkage and rebill
If the original coding is supported, send records and appeal

title: Diagnosis does not match provider type
plain: The payer says the diagnosis is not consistent with the type of provider or specialty that billed the service.
causes: Rendering provider specialty does not match the diagnosis
Wrong provider or NPI on the claim
Payer enrollment specialty mismatch
Diagnosis code outside the provider's scope
fix: Verify the rendering provider NPI, taxonomy, and specialty on the claim
Correct the provider or diagnosis if wrong and rebill
If the service is within scope, appeal with documentation

title: Death date before service date
plain: The payer's records show the patient died before the date of service, so it cannot pay the claim as billed.
causes: Incorrect date of death on file
Wrong patient or member ID used
Wrong date of service on the claim
Patient was deceased before the service
fix: Verify patient identity and the date of death with the family or facility
Correct the claim if the DOS or patient ID is wrong
If the patient was alive, send proof and appeal

title: Birth date after service date
plain: The date of birth on the claim is later than the service date, which is not possible for the patient who received care.
causes: Typo in the patient's date of birth
Wrong date of service on the claim
Wrong patient or member ID used
Payer has an incorrect DOB on file
fix: Check the patient's DOB against the insurance card and chart
Correct the claim and rebill if demographics are wrong
If the payer's file is wrong, appeal with proof of DOB

title: Missing or invalid claim information
plain: The claim is missing required data or contains a billing/submission error, so the payer cannot process it as submitted.
causes: Missing modifier, NDC, referring provider, or authorization number
Invalid or mismatched claim data
Missing diagnosis pointer or service line detail
Typographical or formatting error on the claim
fix: Read the RARC on the remittance for the specific missing item
Correct the claim data and submit a corrected claim
If the payer is wrong, appeal with the supporting information

title: Exact duplicate claim or service
plain: The payer has already received or processed the same claim/service, so this submission is treated as an exact duplicate. This code is usually paired with group code OA, except workers' compensation may use CO.
causes: Same claim was submitted more than once
Corrected claim was not marked as a correction
Claim was resubmitted while the original was still being processed
Payer matched it to an earlier paid claim
fix: Check the prior remittance to see if the original claim paid
If it is a true duplicate, stop billing it
If it is a correction, resubmit with the correct frequency/resubmission code
If it is not a duplicate, appeal with documentation

title: Work injury is workers' comp liability
plain: The payer says the injury or illness is work-related, so the workers' compensation carrier should be responsible for the bill.
causes: Patient reported a work-related injury
Claim indicates employment connection
Employer or workers' comp coverage exists
Payer identified a work injury from claim data
fix: Confirm whether the injury is truly work-related
Bill the workers' compensation carrier if it is
If it is not work-related, appeal with supporting documentation

title: Injury covered by liability carrier
plain: The payer says this injury or illness is covered by a liability carrier, such as auto or premises insurance, rather than by this plan.
causes: Injury involved a third party or accident
Patient has liability coverage
Claim data suggests another party is responsible
Liability carrier should be primary
fix: Verify the liability carrier and policy information
Bill the liability carrier first
If no liability coverage applies, appeal with documentation

title: Injury is no-fault carrier liability
plain: The payer says this injury or illness should be paid by a no-fault carrier, such as auto no-fault insurance.
causes: Auto accident in a no-fault state
Patient has no-fault/PIP coverage
Claim indicates a motor vehicle accident
No-fault carrier should be primary
fix: Confirm the no-fault carrier and claim information
Bill the no-fault carrier first
If no no-fault coverage applies, appeal with documentation

title: Other payer may cover per COB
plain: The payer believes another insurance plan may be responsible for this care under coordination of benefits.
causes: Patient has other active insurance
COB information is missing or outdated
Another payer may be primary
Claim was not billed with COB order
fix: Update coordination of benefits information with the payer
Bill the other payer and obtain their remittance
Rebill this payer with the other payer's explanation of benefits
If no other coverage exists, appeal with proof

title: Prior payer adjudication impact
plain: This adjustment shows how a previous payer already handled the claim, including any payments or adjustments they made. It is used when another payer's remittance is being passed along, not as a new denial from the current payer.
causes: Another payer processed the claim first
Coordination of benefits ordered the prior payer to pay
The current payer is reflecting the prior payer's allowed amount or payment
fix: Review the prior payer's EOB or 835 for the original payment and adjustments
Post the prior payer's payment and adjustments correctly
Bill the secondary or current payer with the correct COB information if needed

title: Covered under capitation plan
plain: The service is included in a capitation or managed care arrangement, so the plan does not pay separately for it. The provider is expected to get compensation through the capitation agreement instead of fee-for-service.
causes: Patient is enrolled in a capitated plan
Service is part of a global capitation payment
Provider is contracted under a managed care arrangement that covers this service
fix: Verify the patient's plan type and capitation arrangement
Check if the service is included in the capitated rate
If not capitated, submit a corrected claim or appeal with contract details

title: Service before coverage began
plain: The date of service is earlier than the patient's coverage start date, so the plan is not responsible for the charges. The patient may owe for the service unless they had other coverage at that time.
causes: Service date is before the policy effective date
Coverage was not active yet on the date of service
Patient's plan start date is later than the visit
fix: Check the patient's coverage effective date
If coverage began later, verify whether the patient had other insurance at the time
Bill the patient or the correct payer for the date of service
If coverage was retroactive, submit a corrected claim with proof

title: Service after coverage ended
plain: The date of service is after the patient's coverage termination date, so the plan is not responsible. The patient may owe for the service unless they had other coverage then.
causes: Service date is after policy termination date
Coverage was cancelled before the visit
Patient's plan ended earlier than the date of service
fix: Check the patient's coverage termination date
Confirm whether the patient had other insurance on the date of service
Bill the patient or the correct payer
If termination was retroactive or in error, submit a corrected claim or appeal

title: Timely filing limit expired
plain: The claim was submitted after the payer's deadline for filing, so the payer is denying it. The provider may not bill the patient for the denied amount in many cases.
causes: Claim was filed too late
Missing or delayed documentation held up submission
Payer's filing limit was shorter than expected
fix: Check the payer's timely filing limit and the claim submission date
Gather proof of timely filing, such as a clearinghouse report or prior submission
Submit an appeal with proof if it was filed on time
If late, write off or follow contract rules before billing the patient

title: Patient not identified as insured
plain: The payer cannot find the patient as a covered member under the policy. This usually means the insurance information is wrong or the patient is not on that plan.
causes: Incorrect member ID or name
Patient is not enrolled in the plan
Policy was terminated or never active
Insurance card was for a different person
fix: Verify the patient's insurance card and member ID
Check eligibility with the payer before rebilling
Update the claim with correct insurance information
If the patient has other coverage, bill the correct payer

title: Not an eligible dependent
plain: The payer's records show the patient does not qualify as a dependent on the policy. This could be due to age, relationship, or plan rules.
causes: Patient is over the dependent age limit
Patient is not a legal dependent under the plan
Dependent coverage was terminated
Incorrect date of birth or relationship on file
fix: Verify dependent eligibility with the payer
Check the policy's dependent age and relationship rules
Update the claim with correct dependent information
If eligibility exists, appeal with proof

title: No dependent coverage on policy
plain: The policy does not include coverage for dependents, so the patient cannot be covered under this plan. The insured may need to add dependent coverage or use another plan.
causes: Policy is individual-only and does not cover dependents
Dependent was never added to the plan
Coverage for dependents was removed
fix: Check the policy's dependent coverage rules
Ask the insured to add the dependent if allowed
Bill the patient or another plan if no dependent coverage exists
Document the denial and notify the patient

title: No newborn coverage on policy
plain: The payer says the insured's policy does not cover newborn care. This may happen if the newborn was not enrolled within the plan's deadline or the plan excludes newborn coverage.
causes: Newborn was not added to the policy within the required timeframe
Policy does not include newborn coverage
Insured has a plan type that excludes newborns
fix: Verify the plan's newborn enrollment rules and deadline
Check if the newborn was added timely
Submit enrollment or a corrected claim with the newborn's information
If not covered, bill the patient or other coverage

title: Lifetime benefit maximum reached
plain: The patient has used up the lifetime maximum benefit allowed under the plan for this type of coverage. The plan will not pay further for these services.
causes: Patient's total benefits have hit the plan's lifetime cap
Plan has a lifetime limit on this benefit
Accumulated claims have exhausted the maximum
fix: Verify the lifetime maximum and amount used with the payer
Check if the plan has any exceptions or restored benefits
Determine if the patient has other coverage or can self-pay
Notify the patient of the benefit exhaustion

title: Authorization or pre-certification denied
plain: The payer denied the service at the time the authorization or pre-certification was requested. Because approval was refused when the request was made, the service is not payable as billed.
causes: Authorization or pre-certification request was denied at the time it was submitted
Service did not meet payer approval criteria
Payer determined the requested service was not approvable under the plan
Denial was issued on the authorization request rather than after claim review
fix: Check the authorization denial reason and payer policy
Obtain retro-authorization if the plan allows it
Submit an appeal with clinical documentation
Rebill with correct authorization or adjust the account

title: Does not qualify as urgent or emergency
plain: The payer says the charges do not meet its rules for emergency or urgent care. The visit or service is being treated as non-urgent or not qualifying for that benefit.
causes: Diagnosis or documentation does not support urgent or emergency care
Payer criteria for emergent or urgent care were not met
Service could have been provided in a non-urgent setting
fix: Review the payer emergency and urgent care policy
Gather clinical notes showing acute symptoms and timing
Appeal with documentation supporting urgent or emergency need
If appropriate, rebill under the correct non-urgent benefit

title: Prompt-pay discount applied
plain: The payer reduced payment because a prompt-pay discount applies. This is a contracted discount for paying the claim within a certain time, not a denial of the service.
causes: Contract includes a prompt-pay discount
Payer paid within the prompt-pay window
Discount was applied to the allowed amount
fix: Post the amount as a contractual adjustment
Verify the discount against the payer contract
Do not bill the patient for the discount
Contact the payer if the discount appears incorrect

title: Charge exceeds allowed amount
plain: The billed charge is higher than the payer fee schedule, maximum allowable, or contracted or legislated rate. The difference is adjusted rather than paid.
causes: Charge exceeds fee schedule
Contracted rate is lower than billed charge
Maximum allowable amount applied
Legislated fee arrangement limits payment
fix: Compare charge to contracted fee schedule
Post correct contractual write-off or patient responsibility based on group code
Appeal if the allowed amount is incorrect
Do not duplicate prior payer adjustments

title: Routine or preventive service not covered
plain: The service is not covered because the payer classifies it as a routine or preventive exam, or as a screening or diagnostic test done with a routine or preventive exam. The plan may exclude routine or preventive care or apply specific benefits.
causes: Service is routine or preventive under plan rules
Screening or diagnostic procedure linked to preventive exam
Preventive benefit not covered or exhausted
fix: Check the patient preventive and routine benefits
Review the Healthcare Policy Identification Segment if present
Bill the patient if the plan excludes the service and notice was given
Appeal if the service should be covered as diagnostic

title: Not medically necessary
plain: The payer considers the service not medically necessary. It is denying coverage because the service does not meet the plan medical necessity criteria.
causes: Payer medical policy says service is not necessary
Documentation does not support medical necessity
Service is not indicated for the diagnosis
Less invasive or alternative service should have been used
fix: Review the payer medical necessity policy
Send clinical notes and supporting documentation
Appeal with a physician letter and records
Consider a peer-to-peer review

title: Pre-existing condition exclusion
plain: The payer is denying the service because it considers the condition pre-existing. The plan may exclude treatment for conditions that existed before coverage began.
causes: Plan has a pre-existing condition exclusion
Diagnosis is considered pre-existing by the payer
No proof of prior continuous coverage
Condition was treated before policy start
fix: Verify plan pre-existing condition rules
Send evidence of prior coverage or symptom onset
Appeal with medical records and a timeline
Bill the patient only if allowed by the plan and law

title: Family or household provider exclusion
plain: The payer does not cover services provided by an immediate relative or someone in the patient household. This is a provider-of-service exclusion.
causes: Provider is related to the patient
Provider lives in the same household as the patient
Plan excludes services from family or household members
fix: Verify the relationship and plan exclusion
Have the patient use a non-related provider
Do not bill the payer for excluded services
Bill the patient only if permitted and disclosed

title: Multiple physicians or assistants not covered
plain: The payer is denying coverage because multiple physicians or assistants are not covered for this case. It may only pay one provider for the service.
causes: Assistant surgeon billed but not covered
Multiple physicians billed for the same service or date
Concurrent care not covered
Only the primary surgeon allowed
fix: Review documentation for distinct services
Bill only the covered primary provider
Use appropriate modifiers if assistants are covered
Appeal with the operative report if separate services were performed

title: Experimental or investigational service
plain: The payer considers the procedure, treatment, or drug experimental or investigational. It is denying coverage because the service is not recognized as proven therapy under the plan.
causes: Service is on the payer experimental or investigational list
Drug lacks FDA approval for this use
Not supported by accepted medical evidence
Clinical trial or unproven treatment
fix: Review the payer experimental and investigational policy
Provide published literature and clinical evidence
Appeal with physician rationale and records
Check if clinical trial or exception coverage applies

title: Procedure not proven effective
plain: The payer considers this procedure or treatment experimental, investigational, or not proven effective, so it is not covered under the plan. The 835 may include a healthcare policy segment pointing to the specific coverage rule.
causes: Procedure is considered experimental or investigational
Payer policy excludes the treatment as not proven effective
Clinical documentation does not establish effectiveness
fix: Review the payer policy and any 835 healthcare policy segment for the specific rule
Check whether the service meets coverage criteria and gather supporting clinical documentation
Correct and resubmit with documentation if coverage criteria are met
If not covered, appeal or follow plan rules for patient liability

title: Inappropriate or invalid place of service
plain: The payer will not pay because the service was rendered in a place of service that is not valid or appropriate for that procedure. This is often a claim coding issue or a setting restriction.
causes: Wrong place of service code on the claim
Service performed in a non-covered setting
Payer policy restricts the procedure to certain settings
fix: Verify the correct place of service code for where the service was performed
Correct the claim and resubmit
If the place of service was correct, appeal with documentation of the setting
Update front desk or scheduling workflows to use appropriate settings

title: Multiple or concurrent procedure bundling
plain: The payer applied multiple procedure or concurrent procedure rules, so payment was reduced or denied for overlapping or bundled services. Examples include multiple surgeries, same-day diagnostic imaging, and concurrent anesthesia.
causes: Multiple surgical procedures billed together
Diagnostic imaging performed on the same day
Concurrent anesthesia services
Procedures the payer considers bundled
fix: Review the multiple procedure rules and any 835 policy segment
Check whether modifiers or documentation support separate payment
Correct coding or modifiers and resubmit
Appeal with operative or procedure documentation if services were distinct

title: Outpatient services around inpatient stay
plain: Outpatient services are not covered when they fall within a specified period before or after an inpatient stay. The payer may require these services to be included with the inpatient claim instead.
causes: Outpatient service provided too close to an inpatient admission or discharge
Payer's global billing period for the inpatient stay
Service should have been included in the inpatient claim
fix: Check the dates of the inpatient and outpatient services
Determine whether the outpatient service should be combined with the inpatient claim
Correct and resubmit the claim or appeal with medical records
Verify the payer's billing and timely filing rules

title: No second surgical opinion
plain: The claim was adjusted because a required second surgical opinion was not obtained before the surgery. The payer may require this as a condition of coverage.
causes: Second opinion not obtained before surgery
Documentation of the second opinion not submitted
Payer requires a second opinion for this procedure
fix: Obtain and document the second surgical opinion if still possible
Submit the second opinion with a corrected claim or appeal
If it cannot be obtained, appeal with an explanation
Update pre-operative checklists to include second opinion requirements

title: Patient blood deductible amount
plain: This is the deductible amount the patient owes for blood or blood products under the plan. The payer is applying a specific blood deductible benefit.
causes: Patient has not met the blood deductible
Blood products were furnished during the stay or procedure
Plan applies a separate blood deductible
fix: Verify the patient's blood deductible benefit
Bill the patient for the blood deductible amount
Apply payments to the deductible
Explain to the patient that this is a plan benefit requirement

title: Day outlier amount
plain: This is a day outlier adjustment: the inpatient stay ran longer than the payer's day outlier threshold, so payment was adjusted (usually increased) to account for the extra days. It is a payment calculation, not a denial of care.
causes: Length of stay exceeds the day outlier threshold
Payer's outlier payment methodology
Additional days are eligible for an outlier adjustment
fix: Review the outlier calculation and the 835 details
Verify the length of stay and patient status
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Cost outlier adjustment
plain: This is a cost outlier adjustment: the case cost far more than usual, so the payer adjusted payment (typically adding an amount) to compensate for costs above the plan's cost outlier threshold. It is a payment calculation for high-cost cases, not a denial.
causes: Costs exceed the cost outlier threshold
Payer's cost outlier payment policy
High-cost case reviewed for additional payment
fix: Review the cost outlier calculation
Verify charges and any supporting cost data
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Indirect medical education adjustment
plain: This is a payment adjustment for indirect medical education costs associated with teaching hospitals. It reflects the additional costs of operating a teaching facility.
causes: Teaching hospital indirect medical education adjustment
Payer's indirect medical education calculation
Claim processed under teaching hospital payment rules
fix: Verify the facility's teaching status and indirect medical education eligibility
Review the indirect medical education adjustment calculation
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Direct medical education adjustment
plain: This is a payment adjustment for direct medical education costs, such as resident training, at teaching facilities. It reflects allowable direct costs of medical education programs.
causes: Teaching hospital direct medical education adjustment
Payer's direct medical education calculation
Claim processed under teaching hospital payment rules
fix: Verify the facility's teaching status and direct medical education eligibility
Review the direct medical education adjustment calculation
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Disproportionate Share Adjustment
plain: An adjustment applied to the payment for hospitals that serve a high share of low-income patients (DSH). It reflects a regulatory payment adjustment, not a denial of the service.
causes: Hospital qualifies for DSH payment
DSH percentage applied to the claim
Payment reconciliation or settlement
fix: Review the remittance advice for the DSH adjustment amount
Verify the DSH percentage and eligibility with the payer
Correct and rebill if the adjustment appears incorrect

title: Non-covered days or room adjustment
plain: An adjustment for days or room charges that the plan does not cover. The non-covered portion may be written off or billed to the patient depending on the plan and any notice given.
causes: Benefit days exhausted
Room type or level of care not covered
No authorization for additional days
fix: Check the plan's benefit limits for days and room type
Appeal with clinical documentation if days were medically necessary
Bill the patient only if they were properly notified of non-coverage

title: Patient Interest Adjustment
plain: An adjustment for interest that the patient owes. The PR group code means the amount is the patient's responsibility.
causes: Late payment by the patient
Plan assesses interest on patient balance
Billing system applied interest in error
fix: Verify the interest amount and the reason it was charged
Collect the interest from the patient if valid
Remove the interest if it was applied incorrectly

title: Professional fees removed from charges
plain: Professional fees were removed from the billed charges, usually because they are billed separately or are included in another payment. This is often a bundling or global billing adjustment.
causes: Global billing split between facility and professional
Professional component not covered under the institutional claim
Duplicate professional charges on the claim
fix: Verify whether the professional fees should be billed separately
Submit a corrected claim or separate professional claim if appropriate
Appeal if the removal was incorrect

title: Ingredient cost adjustment
plain: An adjustment to the ingredient cost of a drug. It applies only to pharmaceuticals and reflects a change from the billed ingredient cost.
causes: Drug pricing update or fee schedule change
Ingredient cost billed differs from the plan's allowance
Contract rate for the drug
fix: Verify the drug's ingredient cost against the plan's fee schedule
Check for a pricing update or contract rate
Appeal with supporting documentation if the adjustment is incorrect

title: Dispensing fee adjustment
plain: An adjustment to the dispensing fee for a pharmaceutical. It changes the amount allowed for dispensing the drug.
causes: Dispensing fee differs from the plan's fee schedule
Contract rate for dispensing
Incorrect dispensing fee billed
fix: Compare the billed dispensing fee to the plan's allowed amount
Verify the contract or fee schedule
Appeal if the adjustment is incorrect

title: Processed in excess of charges
plain: The claim was processed, but the allowed amount is higher than the billed charges. Payment is limited to the charges, so the excess is not paid.
causes: Billed charge is lower than the plan's allowed amount
Provider underbilled the service
Charge entry error
fix: Verify the billed charges are correct
Correct and rebill if charges were understated
Accept the adjustment if charges were correct

title: Plan procedures not followed
plain: The plan's rules or procedures were not followed, such as obtaining prior authorization or a referral. The claim may be denied or reduced.
causes: No prior authorization obtained
No referral on file
Out-of-network without plan approval
Wrong process followed for the service
fix: Identify which plan procedure was missed
Obtain retro-authorization or a referral if allowed
Appeal with documentation showing the procedure was followed or was not required

title: Non-covered charge denial
plain: The service or item is not covered by the patient's plan. A remark code must also be provided to explain why it is not covered.
causes: Service not included in the benefit plan
Experimental or investigational service
Not medically necessary
Service excluded under plan terms (e.g., cosmetic or convenience item)
fix: Read the required remark code for the specific reason
Verify the patient's benefits and coverage
Appeal with medical necessity documentation if appropriate
Bill the patient only if they were properly notified of non-coverage

title: Service included in another payment
plain: This service is bundled into another service or procedure that was already paid. The plan considers it part of the primary service's payment.
causes: Service is integral to a primary procedure
Global surgical package includes the service
Duplicate component of a paid service
Bundling edit applied by the payer
fix: Review the bundling edit and the primary service paid
Appeal with a modifier or documentation if the service should be paid separately
Write off the bundled amount if the adjustment is correct — do not bill the patient for a contractual (CO) adjustment

title: Payment sent to patient
plain: The payer sent the payment to the patient or another responsible party instead of the provider. The provider may need to collect from that party.
causes: Payer sent reimbursement directly to patient
Patient has a direct payment arrangement
Provider did not accept assignment
fix: Verify whether patient received payment
Bill patient for the amount if appropriate
Update remittance address or assignment status with payer

title: Predetermination anticipated payment
plain: This is a pre-service estimate of the payment the payer expects to make once the service is done or the claim is finalized. It is not a final payment or denial.
causes: Predetermination request submitted
Payer provides advance coverage estimate
Claim not yet final adjudicated
fix: Use estimate for planning only
Submit claim after services are completed
Review final remittance for actual payment

title: Major medical adjustment
plain: The payer adjusted the amount under the major medical part of the health plan. This reflects how major medical benefits were applied.
causes: Service processed under major medical benefits
Plan applies major medical deductible or coinsurance
Coordination between medical and major medical benefits
fix: Check plan benefits for major medical coverage
Verify deductible and coinsurance amounts
Rebill if adjustment appears incorrect

title: Provider promotional discount
plain: The provider chose to give a promotional discount, such as a senior citizen discount. The adjustment shows the discounted amount, which the provider absorbs rather than bills to the payer or patient.
causes: Provider offers senior citizen discount
Promotional pricing applied
Contract includes discount provision
fix: Confirm discount was intended
Adjust patient billing to reflect discount
Remove discount if applied in error

title: Managed care withholding
plain: The payer withheld part of the payment under a managed care contract. The withheld amount may be paid later if contract conditions are met.
causes: Managed care contract requires withholding
Risk pool or incentive arrangement
Withholding for quality or utilization targets
fix: Review contract withholding terms
Track withheld amounts for future reconciliation
Contact payer if withholding seems incorrect

title: Tax withholding
plain: The payer withheld funds for taxes from the payment. This can happen when the law or contract requires tax withholding.
causes: Tax withholding required by law
Contract requires tax withholding
Payer withholds taxes from payment
fix: Verify tax withholding requirements
Check contract for tax withholding terms
Consult tax advisor if needed

title: Patient payment election inactive
plain: The patient's selected payment option or election is not active for this claim. This may affect how the patient balance is handled.
causes: Patient's payment election expired
Election not active on date of service
Payer did not apply patient's option
fix: Verify patient's current payment election
Contact patient to update election
Rebill or adjust based on active option

title: Related claim not identified
plain: The claim or service depends on another claim or qualifying service, but that related claim was not referenced on this claim. The payer cannot process it as related without that information.
causes: Missing prior claim number
Related service not linked
Incorrect or omitted reference number
fix: Identify the related claim or service
Add the correct reference number to the claim
Resubmit the claim with the required information

title: Rent/purchase guidelines not met
plain: The payer's rules for renting or buying equipment were not satisfied. This may be due to missing documentation or criteria not being met.
causes: Missing rental/purchase documentation
Equipment does not meet payer guidelines
Wrong rental versus purchase billing
fix: Review payer's rent/purchase guidelines
Obtain and submit missing documentation
Correct billing to rent or purchase as appropriate

title: Not covered by this payer
plain: This payer is not responsible for the claim or service, so it will not pay. The biller needs to send the claim to the payer that actually covers the patient or this service.
causes: Wrong payer billed
Patient's coverage changed
Payer not contracted for this service
fix: Verify patient's current insurance
Identify the correct payer
Submit the claim to the correct payer

title: Billing date before service date
plain: The claim shows a billing date that is earlier than the date the service was provided. That date order is not valid for processing the claim.
causes: Billing date keyed before the date of service
System default date is incorrect
Date fields entered in the wrong order
fix: Verify the actual date of service
Correct the billing date on the claim
Resubmit the corrected claim

title: Not covered without assignment
plain: This service is covered only if the provider agrees to accept assignment. Because that agreement was not in place, the service is not covered as billed.
causes: Provider did not accept assignment
Assignment agreement missing from the claim
Provider is not participating for this service
fix: Confirm whether the provider will accept assignment
Obtain and document the assignment agreement
Resubmit the claim with assignment or handle per policy

title: Service not direct or documented
plain: The service was not furnished directly to the patient, or there is no documentation showing it was provided. The payer needs proof that the service happened and was for the patient.
causes: No documentation showing the service was furnished
Service was provided by someone other than the billing provider
Service was not delivered directly to the patient
fix: Obtain and attach supporting documentation
Verify the performing provider and correct the claim
Resubmit with proof of direct service

title: Procedure not FDA approved
plain: The procedure or product has not been approved by the FDA. The payer does not cover items that lack FDA approval.
causes: Drug, device, or product lacks FDA approval
Off-label use not covered by policy
Investigational or experimental item
fix: Check FDA approval status
Review coverage policy for exceptions
Appeal with clinical documentation if appropriate

title: Procedure canceled, postponed, or delayed
plain: The procedure was postponed, canceled, or delayed, so the payer is not paying for it as billed. This usually means the service was not actually performed on the date claimed.
causes: Procedure was canceled
Procedure was postponed
Procedure was delayed and not performed as billed
fix: Confirm whether the service was actually performed
Do not bill for canceled or postponed services
If performed on a different date, correct and resubmit the claim

title: Invalid advance notice from patient
plain: The advance notice signed by the patient does not meet the payer's requirements. Without a valid notice, the provider cannot hold the patient responsible for the service.
causes: Advance notice missing or incomplete
Patient signature missing or invalid
Notice did not meet required wording or timing
fix: Review the notice for compliance
Obtain a valid signed notice if possible
If not valid, write off the service or correct per policy

title: Transportation not to closest facility
plain: The plan pays for transportation only to the nearest facility capable of treating the patient's condition. This claim was adjusted because the patient was taken to a more distant facility, so the extra distance is not payable.
causes: Patient chose a facility farther than the closest capable facility
Closest facility was not used without medical justification
Transportation exceeded covered distance
fix: Verify the closest appropriate facility
Obtain documentation of medical need for the farther facility
Appeal with supporting records
Bill the patient for the noncovered portion if allowed

title: ESRD network support adjustment
plain: This is an adjustment for ESRD network support. It is a required payment adjustment, not a denial of the service itself.
causes: ESRD network support adjustment applied
Mandatory adjustment for ESRD network
Payer applied a support fee or adjustment
fix: Post the adjustment to the claim
Verify ESRD network status
No appeal needed unless the adjustment is incorrect

title: Benefit maximum reached
plain: The patient has used up the maximum amount the plan will pay for this service during the current benefit period or for this episode of care. No further benefits are available under that limit.
causes: Annual or lifetime benefit maximum reached
Visit or occurrence limit reached
Benefit period maximum exhausted
fix: Verify the patient's benefit maximum
Bill the patient for the noncovered amount if appropriate
Appeal if the maximum was applied incorrectly

title: Indemnification adjustment for member responsibility
plain: This is an indemnification adjustment to compensate the provider for a member responsibility that is still outstanding. It adjusts the claim to account for that amount.
causes: Payer is compensating provider for outstanding member responsibility
Indemnification adjustment applied
Member responsibility not collected
fix: Post the adjustment
Verify the member responsibility amount
Follow up on any remaining balance

title: Reduction applied to psychiatric services
plain: The payer reduced what it paid for a psychiatric service, applying a plan or contract limit that lowers the allowed amount for behavioral-health treatment. It is not a statement that the service was unnecessary, just that psychiatric charges are paid at a reduced rate.
causes: Plan benefit applies a lower payment rate for psychiatric/behavioral health services
Contract caps or reduces reimbursement for mental health codes
Reduction taken instead of, or in addition to, the normal fee schedule
fix: Read the remark codes on the same line to see which benefit limit was applied
Check the member's behavioral-health benefit and the provider's contracted psych rate
Verify the CPT/HCPCS code billed reflects the correct service level
If the reduction is wrong, appeal with the fee schedule or contract page cited

title: Newborn care included in mother's payment
plain: The services billed for a newborn were treated as already paid inside the mother's maternity allowance, so the payer issued no separate payment. Newborn care usually has to be billed on the baby's own enrollment and policy, not the mother's.
causes: Newborn charged under the mother's claim or member ID instead of the baby's own record
Newborn not yet added to the plan, so the payer bundled the care into the mother's allowance
Facility billed routine newborn care as part of the mother's global maternity payment
fix: Confirm the newborn has his or her own member ID; if not, help the family complete the enrollment
Rebill the newborn services under the baby's own name, date of birth, and policy number
If the plan does not issue a separate newborn ID, request written instructions and resubmit as directed
Appeal with the birth record and enrollment documentation if the plan still denies

title: Prior processing data looks wrong
plain: The payer believes the information your claim carried about earlier processing (such as what a prior payer or prior claim allowed, paid, or adjusted) does not add up. A remark code must accompany this code to explain what specifically looks off.
causes: Incorrect prior payer allowed, paid, or adjustment amounts entered on the claim
Stale or mismatched prior remittance data from an earlier adjudication
Corrected or replacement claim submitted without updating the prior processing fields
fix: Read the attached remark code to see exactly which prior-processing element is flagged
Pull the prior EOB/835 and re-key the allowed, paid, and adjustment amounts exactly
Correct the prior payer ID, claim number, and dates if they do not match
Resubmit as a corrected claim with the corrected prior-processing detail

title: Fee charged for claim submission
plain: A fee was taken out for submitting the claim — for example a payer or clearinghouse charge for processing the submission. It reduces the payment rather than denying the service itself.
causes: Clearinghouse or vendor per-claim submission fee passed through by the payer
Plan or intermediary charges a processing fee per claim
Fee written into the participation agreement or vendor contract
fix: Check the payer or clearinghouse contract to confirm the fee is authorized
Confirm the fee amount matches the agreed per-claim rate
If the fee is not in the contract, appeal and request the deduction be reversed
Adjust internal fee schedules or vendor terms so expected reimbursement is accurate

title: Negotiated discount on this claim
plain: The payer applied a discount that was negotiated specifically for this claim, lowering the amount paid below the billed charge. This is a contract-driven write-off, not a dispute about the service.
causes: Single-case or claim-specific rate agreement between payer and provider
Contract provision allowing a discount on this particular claim or service
Multi-payer or bundled-rate arrangement applied at adjudication
fix: Confirm the discount matches the signed claim-specific or case-rate agreement
Post the difference as a contractual adjustment, not patient responsibility
If the discount is larger than agreed, appeal with the signed agreement attached
Update the expected-reimbursement calculation for similar claims

title: Adjustment for prearranged demonstration project
plain: Payment was adjusted because the claim falls under a demonstration or pilot project with its own prearranged payment rules. The adjustment reflects the project's terms rather than standard plan pricing.
causes: Provider or member enrolled in a CMS or payer demonstration/pilot program
Services delivered under an alternative payment model with special rates
Project-specific payment rules applied instead of standard fee schedule
fix: Confirm the patient or provider is actually participating in the named project
Obtain the project's payment methodology and verify the adjustment math
Post any shortfall per the project's rules rather than billing the patient
Appeal with project documentation if the adjustment does not match the stated terms

title: Service line still under review
plain: The payer has not finished deciding about this line and no final payment decision has been made yet. It is paired with Group Code OA and must be reversed and corrected once the review is complete.
causes: Line pulled for medical review, audit, or additional internal review
Documentation or clinical information requested but not yet received
Adjudication held while the payer resolves a conflict on the claim
fix: Send any documentation or records the payer requested as soon as possible
Track the line and watch for the final remittance that replaces this pending status
Do not bill the patient for this line while it is still open
If no decision arrives within the payer's stated timeframe, follow up or escalate

title: Technical component removed from charges
plain: The technical portion of the service was stripped from what was billed because the payer considers it already covered elsewhere — typically inside a facility payment or a global service. Only the professional piece, if any, remains payable here.
causes: Technical component billed separately when the facility already gets paid for it
Global code submitted where the payer only allows the professional portion
Duplicate billing of the technical piece by both a facility and a professional
fix: Rebill the professional portion only, using modifier 26 where appropriate
Route the technical component to the correct payer or facility claim
Confirm which entity owns the technical component under the patient's plan
Adjust the charge to remove the technical piece so the claim matches the allowed service

title: Interim bill cannot be processed
plain: The payer does not accept an interim or periodic bill for this stay; it wants one final bill covering the completed episode of care. Payment waits until the final claim is submitted.
causes: Monthly or interim hospital/facility bill submitted before discharge
Payer policy requires a single final claim for the entire stay
Interim billing used when the payer only accepts final bills for that service type
fix: Hold interim charges until the episode of care is complete
Combine all dates of service into a single final claim and submit it
Check the payer's billing rules for whether interim bills are ever accepted
Keep the interim bill on file for reconciliation against the final claim

title: Prior payer's coverage rules not followed
plain: The claim did not follow the coverage rules of the payer that processed it earlier, so this payer will not pay its share yet. The earlier payer's requirements — such as order of benefits or required steps — must be met first. Per the official definition, this code may only appear with Group Code OA (other adjustment).
causes: Primary and secondary payers billed in the wrong order
Required prior authorization, referral, or network rules from the first payer were skipped
Claim submitted without documenting that the prior payer's conditions were satisfied
fix: Obtain the prior payer's coverage rules or denial notice and read the specific requirement
Correct the order of benefits or complete the missing step with the prior payer
Resubmit with the prior payer's EOB/denial attached as proof
Coordinate directly with the prior payer if the requirement is unclear

title: Regulatory surcharge or health tax adjustment
plain: This adjustment reflects a government-mandated surcharge, assessment, allowance, or health-related tax. It is not a statement that the service itself was denied.
causes: State or federal health-related tax
Regulatory assessment or surcharge
Allowance required by law or regulation
fix: Confirm the surcharge or tax applies to this claim
Reconcile the adjustment with the applicable fee schedule or contract
Post the adjustment and balance the remittance

title: Subscriber employed by provider
plain: The subscriber is employed by the provider, so the claim is handled under a contracted funding agreement. This code is used only with group code CO.
causes: Patient or subscriber works for the provider
A contracted funding agreement applies
Payer processed the claim under that agreement
fix: Verify the subscriber's employment with the provider
Confirm the contracted funding agreement terms
Correct and resubmit the claim if the agreement does not apply

title: Patient ID and name mismatch
plain: The health identification number and the patient or insured name on the claim do not match the payer's records. The claim cannot be processed until the identifying information agrees.
causes: Typo in the member ID or name
Patient name changed but records were not updated
Wrong member ID used for the patient
Eligibility file does not match the claim
fix: Check the patient's ID card and eligibility record
Correct the name or member ID on the claim
Resubmit the corrected claim

title: Monthly Medicaid patient liability
plain: This amount is the patient's monthly Medicaid liability, such as a spenddown or share-of-cost amount. It is the portion the patient may owe for the month.
causes: Medicaid monthly liability or spenddown applies
Patient income or resources create a monthly share
State Medicaid determined a patient liability amount
fix: Verify the monthly liability amount with Medicaid
Bill the patient for the liability as allowed
Document the patient liability notice and payment

title: Portion of payment deferred
plain: The payer has postponed paying part of this claim rather than denying it. The deferred amount may be paid later once review or processing is complete.
causes: Additional review is pending
Payer is waiting for more information
Payment is being withheld temporarily
Coordination of benefits or processing delay
fix: Check the remittance for any remark codes explaining the deferral
Provide any requested information to the payer
Monitor the claim for later payment

title: Preferred product or service incentive
plain: The payer applied an incentive adjustment, for example because a preferred product or service was used. Depending on the program, an incentive adjustment can increase or decrease payment, so compare it with the incentive terms rather than assuming it is a pay cut.
causes: Preferred product or service was used
Contract includes an incentive adjustment
Payer applied an incentive program rate
fix: Check the contract or payer policy for the incentive terms
Confirm the correct product or service was billed
Reconcile the adjustment with the expected payment

title: Diagnosis invalid for date
plain: The diagnosis code on the claim was not valid for the date of service reported. The payer could not accept the diagnosis as billed.
causes: Diagnosis code not effective on the date of service
Outdated or wrong ICD code used
Typo in the diagnosis code
Code deleted or invalid for the reported date
fix: Review the medical record for the correct diagnosis
Select a diagnosis code valid for the date of service
Correct and resubmit the claim

title: Contracted rate expired or missing
plain: The provider's contracted or negotiated rate has expired or is not on file with the payer. The payer does not have a current rate to apply to this service.
causes: Contract has expired
Negotiated rate was not loaded by the payer
Wrong provider or location on the claim
Missing fee schedule information
fix: Verify the contract effective dates and rates
Ask the payer to load the current contracted rate
Correct provider information if needed and resubmit

title: Missing information from another provider
plain: The payer did not receive needed information from another provider, or what was received was insufficient or incomplete. A remark code must be provided to explain what is missing.
causes: Records from another provider were not sent
Documentation from another provider is incomplete
Required clinical information is missing
Payer did not get enough detail to process the claim
fix: Read the required remark code for the specific missing item
Request the needed records from the other provider
Submit the information to the payer and resubmit the claim

title: Lifetime benefit maximum reached
plain: The patient has reached the lifetime maximum benefit for this service or benefit category. The payer will not pay further for this service under that lifetime cap.
causes: Lifetime maximum has been met
Benefit category maximum exhausted
Payer's records show no remaining lifetime benefit
Service is subject to a lifetime cap
fix: Verify the lifetime maximum and amount used
Check whether another benefit category or payer applies
Bill the patient only if allowed after the cap
Appeal if the maximum was calculated incorrectly

title: Service level not supported
plain: The payer says the information or documentation submitted does not justify the level of service billed, such as the E/M visit level or the level of care (for example, inpatient versus observation). This often results in a downcode, a level-of-care downgrade, or denial of the billed level.
causes: Documentation does not support the billed E/M level or complexity
Documentation does not support the billed level of care (for example, inpatient admission criteria not met)
Incorrect level of service code selected
Missing details such as time, history, exam, or medical decision making
fix: Review the encounter note against the code-level criteria
Correct the service level if documentation supports a lower level
Submit an appeal with the complete medical record if the billed level is supported

title: Frequency of services not supported
plain: The payer says the information submitted does not justify how many services were billed or how often they were provided. Payment is adjusted for the unsupported number or frequency of services.
causes: More units or visits billed than the documentation supports
Documentation does not show medical need for the frequency
Payer policy limits the frequency of the service
fix: Compare billed units or visits with the clinical documentation
Correct units or frequency if documentation is insufficient
Appeal with records showing the medical need for the frequency

title: Length of service not supported
plain: The payer says the documentation submitted does not support the length of service billed, such as the number of inpatient days or the duration of a time-based service. When this code appears, check the 835 remittance for a Healthcare Policy Identification Segment (Loop 2110 REF), which may identify the specific payer policy applied.
causes: Inpatient length of stay not supported by the medical record
Time-based code billed but time is not documented
Documentation does not support the duration billed
Length exceeds payer policy or plan limit
fix: Check the 835 Healthcare Policy Identification Segment (Loop 2110 REF) for the policy the payer applied
Review the documentation for start/stop times, duration, or inpatient days
Correct the length or units billed
Appeal with records supporting the length of service

title: Dosage not supported
plain: The payer says the information submitted does not justify the dosage billed. Payment is adjusted because the documented dosage does not support the amount billed.
causes: Dosage billed does not match the medication administration record
Documentation does not support the amount given
Payer policy limits the dosage
fix: Check the medication record and the units billed
Correct the dosage or units if wrong
Appeal with documentation supporting the dosage

title: Day supply not supported
plain: The payer says the information submitted does not justify the day's supply billed. Payment is adjusted for the unsupported days-supply amount.
causes: Day supply billed does not match the prescription or documentation
Payer limit on day supply exceeded
Incorrect days-supply calculation
fix: Verify the prescription and days-supply calculation
Correct the days supply on the claim
Appeal with documentation or prescription if the supply is supported

title: Patient refused service
plain: The patient declined the service or procedure, so the payer will not pay for it. In most cases this means the care was not carried out because the patient chose not to receive it.
causes: Patient declined the service at the time of care
Refusal documented in the chart
Service was not performed because of patient refusal
fix: Confirm the refusal is documented in the medical record
Do not rebill the payer for the refused service
Bill the patient only if your policies and plan rules allow

title: Service due to act of war
plain: The care being billed was needed because of an act of war, and the payer is treating it under the plan's coverage exclusion or limitation for war-related treatment.
causes: Injury or illness related to an act of war
Plan excludes services connected to war
Payer applied a benefit exclusion
fix: Review the plan document for the war exclusion
Determine whether the exclusion truly applies
Appeal if the service is misclassified or bill the patient if the exclusion applies

title: Service provided outside United States
plain: The care took place outside the United States, and the payer is limiting or denying payment based on that location. Many plans cover foreign care only in emergencies or not at all.
causes: Care was rendered in a foreign country
Plan excludes non-emergency services outside the U.S.
Payer applied a geographic coverage limit
fix: Check the plan for foreign-care or emergency exceptions
Submit records if an exception applies
Appeal if coverage was denied incorrectly

title: Service due to terrorism
plain: The care being billed stems from an act of terrorism, and the payer is treating it under the plan's coverage exclusion or limitation for terrorism-related treatment.
causes: Injury or illness related to a terrorist act
Plan excludes services connected to terrorism
Payer applied a benefit exclusion
fix: Review the plan document for the terrorism exclusion
Verify whether the exclusion applies to the service
Appeal if the denial is incorrect or bill the patient if the exclusion applies

title: Injury from excluded activity
plain: The patient's injury or illness stems from an activity the plan lists as excluded from coverage (for example, certain high-risk or prohibited activities), so the payer is denying or reducing payment under that benefit exclusion.
causes: Injury occurred during an activity the plan excludes
Documentation links the condition to an excluded activity
Payer applied a benefit exclusion
fix: Review the plan's exclusion list and the clinical record
Confirm whether the activity is actually excluded
Appeal if the exclusion was applied incorrectly

title: Performance bonus added to payment
plain: The payer added extra money on top of the normal payment because the provider met the plan's quality or performance targets. It is not a denial or a takeback.
causes: Provider hit a quality or efficiency target in the payer's program
Value-based or pay-for-performance incentive earned for the period
Bonus calculated on a measure the provider reported to the payer
fix: Post the bonus to the correct period and provider in the practice management system
Reconcile the amount against the payer's incentive report
Contact the payer only if the expected bonus is missing or short

title: Requested documentation never received
plain: The claim pointed to records or attachments the payer needed, but those documents never arrived, so the payer could not review the claim and denied it.
causes: Claim indicated an attachment but nothing was sent
Records went to the wrong fax number or address
Documentation request notice was missed or misfiled
fix: Read the request letter or remark code to see exactly what is needed and where to send it
Pull the records and send them by the method the payer requires, noting the claim number
Resubmit the claim with the documentation attached, or file an appeal within the payer's deadline
Log the response date so the resubmission can be tracked

title: Documentation received after deadline
plain: Same idea as a missing-attachment denial, except the payer did get the records but they arrived after the payer's cutoff date for review.
causes: Medical records took too long to gather from the facility or physician
Documents were mailed instead of sent electronically
Practice was waiting on the patient to supply outside records
fix: Send the documentation immediately and keep proof of the send date
Confirm the payer's documentation deadline for this claim type
Appeal with the records plus an explanation of the delay if the payer allows late submission for good cause
Set internal reminders so documentation requests are answered within a few days

title: Claim submitted after plan responsibility ended
plain: The claim was sent in after this payer's responsibility for processing claims under the plan had already ended — for example, coverage moved to a new carrier and the old plan's run-out window for claims had closed. The problem is the filing date, not the date the service happened.
causes: Plan terminated and the claim was filed after the run-out period closed
Member or employer switched carriers and the claim reached the prior payer too late
Retroactive termination or plan change processed while the claim was still unsubmitted
Claim went to the wrong payer first and arrived after this payer's responsibility ended
fix: Get the plan's termination date and run-out filing rules from the payer or plan documents
Confirm which payer was responsible on the date of service and bill that payer
If the claim was originally submitted on time, appeal with the acceptance report proving the original filing date
If the payer's responsibility truly ended before submission, follow the plan's run-out process or handle the balance per your financial policy

title: Diagnosis is not a covered benefit
plain: The diagnosis submitted with the claim is not covered under this plan, so the related service is denied. Check the healthcare policy segment on the remittance for the exact rule the payer applied.
causes: The condition itself is excluded from the plan's benefit list
The diagnosis code does not support the service that was billed
Diagnosis was coded incorrectly or too vaguely
Payer's medical policy links the service only to certain diagnoses
fix: Review the policy segment on the 835 and compare it to the diagnosis billed
Have the coder confirm the diagnosis reflects what was actually treated and correct it if wrong
Resubmit a corrected claim when the diagnosis was inaccurate
If the diagnosis is correct but excluded, bill the patient as patient responsibility after following notice requirements, or appeal with records supporting coverage

title: Payer substituted a different benefit
plain: Instead of paying for what was billed, the payer provided an alternate benefit — usually a similar but less costly drug, supply, or service — and paid based on that alternate.
causes: Plan policy prefers a different drug, product, or service in the same class
Brand was billed where a generic or preferred item is covered
Quantity, strength, or duration limits pushed the claim to an alternate benefit
Service was delivered in a setting the plan considers interchangeable with another
fix: Read the remittance to identify which alternate benefit was applied
Compare it with what was actually furnished and documented
Appeal with records showing the billed item was necessary and the alternate was tried, failed, or unsuitable
If the alternate stands, adjust the charge to the allowed alternate amount and bill the patient for any remaining balance only if permitted by the plan and your notice policy

title: This provider type is not payable
plain: The plan does not pay for this service when it is performed or billed by this type of provider, no matter the circumstances. The policy segment on the remittance shows the restriction the payer used.
causes: Provider's specialty or taxonomy is not a recognized billing type for this code
Plan benefit excludes services from this provider category
Provider credentialing or enrollment is under a different provider type than billed
Non-participating provider type with no out-of-network benefit
fix: Confirm how the provider is enrolled and what taxonomy was submitted on the claim
Check the policy segment to see whether the restriction is plan-wide or claim-specific
Correct the claim if the provider type or taxonomy was reported wrong
Appeal with credentialing documents or scope-of-practice evidence when payment should apply
If the exclusion is valid, follow your financial policy for billing the patient

title: Not payable for provider and facility combo
plain: The plan refuses to pay this combination: a provider of this type delivering the service in this kind of facility or place of service. Either the provider type, the setting, or the two together fall outside the plan's payment rules — check the healthcare policy segment on the remittance, if present, for the exact restriction applied.
causes: Place of service on the claim does not match the setting allowed for this provider
Plan limits this provider type in hospital, surgical center, or other facility settings
Service was rendered in a location outside the provider's enrolled practice setting
Wrong place-of-service code keyed on the claim
fix: Verify the place of service reported against the documentation and the actual setting
Correct the place of service and resubmit if it was reported in error
Review the policy segment for the specific provider-and-facility restriction
Appeal with facility records if the service legitimately qualifies
If the restriction is correct, move the balance per your self-pay or notice policy

title: Payment reduced for this specialty
plain: The service is covered, but the payer reduced the payment because of the provider's specialty — the plan's allowed amount for this provider type or specialty is lower than what was billed.
causes: Specialty-specific fee schedule applies to this code
Provider billed at a rate above the contracted amount for that specialty
Specialty reported on enrollment or the claim differs from the contracted specialty
Multiple-specialty or ancillary rate tier applied
fix: Compare the paid amount with the contracted fee schedule or rate sheet for this specialty
Fix the specialty or taxonomy on the claim if it was reported incorrectly and resubmit
Update the specialty on file with the payer if enrollment data is wrong
Appeal with the contract page showing the correct rate if the reduction looks wrong
Write off the difference only if the contract requires it

title: No physician prescription on file
plain: The payer denied because the service or equipment was not prescribed by a physician, or the prescription was never supplied to the payer.
causes: No written order exists for the service or item
Order is unsigned, undated, or missing the specific item and quantity
Order was obtained but never sent with the claim or the records
Payer requires a renewed or updated prescription for the time period billed
fix: Ask the treating physician for a signed, dated order covering the item, quantity, and dates of service
Make sure the order meets the payer's content rules before sending it
Send the order with a corrected claim or appeal, referencing the claim number
Track the appeal deadline so the response is filed on time

title: Service not prescribed before delivery
plain: The payer says the item or service was delivered before a valid prescription or order was obtained. A prescription must be in place before the service is provided.
causes: No prescription or order on file before delivery
Prescription dated after the delivery date
Required signed order was not obtained
fix: Obtain a valid prescription or order dated before delivery
Correct the claim with the prescription documentation
Submit a corrected claim or appeal with the order

title: Incomplete prescription on file
plain: The prescription or order on file is missing required information, so the payer cannot process the claim. It may lack details like quantity, directions, diagnosis, or a prescriber signature.
causes: Missing required fields on the prescription
No prescriber signature or NPI
Prescription is illegible or incomplete
fix: Ask the prescriber to complete all missing fields
Obtain a corrected, signed prescription
Resubmit the claim with the complete order

title: Prescription not current
